scene: Narrow climb, southern sky and Belacqua waiting in the shade
story: The passage through the mountain narrows so sharply that Dante and Virgil must climb with their hands and feet, clinging to the rocks.
They emerge onto a ledge, and Dante rests, exhausted. He notices that the sun appears to his left, contrary to the orientation familiar from the northern hemisphere.
Virgil explains that on the mountain in the southern hemisphere the sun's apparent path looks different; Dante considers the geometry of their new position.
After continuing around the slope, they encounter souls resting in the shade. One sits with his knees drawn toward his chest, barely inclined to rise.

Dante recognizes Belacqua, who had delayed repentance while alive. Belacqua remarks on the waiting required before he can reach the gate of Purgatory, unless prayers from a soul in grace shorten that wait.
Virgil urges Dante onward. The living travelers move; Belacqua remains where he is, awaiting his appointed time.
